notes: Summary: Enterprise contact-center provider evaluating Redwood for low-latency streaming chat and real-time summarization.
POC results disappointing — p95 token latency ~1.2s end-to-end (target 200-300ms); streaming arrives in bursts; UI jitter on live agent console.
SE notes: attempted batching and prefix caching; kernel + quantization tuning reduced avg latency slightly but p95 still >800ms in EU region.
Security: QA flagged that streaming endpoints did not produce deterministic audit log entries for partial outputs — blocker for regulated customers.
Customer quote (engineer): 'We saw occasional 200ms medians but the tail kills UX — can't risk that for live calls.'
Commercial: Pricing acceptable but team said a competing vendor (LumenAI) demo showed smoother streaming on live transcripts — customer leaned to them.
Internal: AE pushed Dedicated with colocated nodes and reserved capacity; finance pushed back (Q2 budget freeze) — no internal champion to fight for line item.
Outcome: Stalled in late evaluation, then unresponsive after competitor pilot. Marked as lost-stalled; keep notes for re-engage in 6-9 months.
Follow-ups attempted: 3 outreach emails, one voicemail, one C-level intro via partner; no reply since 2026-02-28.

Recommended next actions: 1) Prepare low-latency reference architecture (EU colocation) 2) Collect p95 mitigation doc + streaming QA checklist 3) Wait 6 months for budget window and attempt executive re-intro.
